title: Unified add-on experimentation framework: pricing gates for retention, compliance pack, and premium SLA
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Build a repeatable experimentation framework to validate price and gating strategies for three add-ons: extended observability retention, a compliance/security questionnaire package, and a premium SLA. This ticket scopes the MVP experiment, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and handoffs for Legal/Revenue/Engineering. We want to learn (1) willingness to pay for retention beyond baseline, (2) buyer sensitivity to a bundled compliance questionnaire + evidence package versus ala carte, and (3) conversion lift from a clearly-gated premium SLA offering. Primary outcomes are revenue uplift, upgrade velocity, and sales friction metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment infra implemented in console and billing layer with A/B variant control
Three price variants instrumented for each add-on (low/mid/high) with consistent metrics collection
UI gating flows built for self-serve and sales-assist paths (console + sales quote template)
Legal sign-off on compliance pack deliverables and contract language for premium SLA
Telemetry: cohort-level upgrade rate, MRR delta, support ticket volume, and churn signal tracked for 30 days post-exposure
success_metrics: Upgrade conversion >= 2.5% in at least one tier OR incremental ARPU >= $250/month for mid tier
No >15% increase in sales cycle length for deals flagged as enterprise
No material spike (>20%) in support requests related to add-on onboarding
Data available for decision after 30 days of experiment exposure
experiment_design_summary: Variant A (Control): baseline product with existing retention and SLA; no explicit compliance add-on messaging
Variant B (Self-serve gating): add-on shown in console as purchasable upgrade with three pricing tiers and clear entitlement text
Variant C (Sales-assist emphasis): same pricing as B but includes ‘sales assist’ CTA and pre-filled security questionnaire template for enterprise contacts
Randomize at account-level with stratification by ARR band and usage pattern (embedding-heavy vs generation-heavy)
pricing_hypotheses: Customers with baseline > $5k ARR are willing to pay for 90-day observability retention at a 10-15% uplift
Compliance pack sells better as a bundled offering with SLA for customers in regulated verticals (finance/healthcare), compared to a la carte documentation
Premium SLA adoption will be limited by perceived implementation effort; offering a canned upgrade path (sales assist + questionnaire) will increase conversion
implementation_notes: Console: new add-ons page UI + modal shown on billing settings; feature flag gated (ENG-21033)
Billing: map add-on SKUs to usage invoice lines; ensure proration handled for mid-cycle upgrades (ENG-21311)
Backend: entitlement toggle in account service and rollout bucket keyed by account id
Design: copy and microcopy to emphasize deliverables in compliance pack and SLA SLOs (DES-4421)
Legal: template contract language and evidence package checklist to be added to Sales playbook
Telemetry: new dashboards in Console Optimize for cohort-level MRR and support signal

decisions: Use account-level randomization rather than user-level to avoid cross-contamination of purchasing behavior
Expose three price points (basic, standard, enterprise) for each add-on to get elasticity curve
Require Legal sign-off on compliance pack artifacts before any commercial offering is displayed
Rollout sales-assist CTA only for segments above $50k ARR and for enterprise contacts flagged in CRM
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales confusion / double-selling. Mitigation: Provide Sales Ops one-pager and quote templates; hide sales CTA for already-contracted accounts
Risk: Billing mapping errors causing invoicing disputes. Mitigation: Staging billing tests and manual review for first 20 upgrades
Risk: Support churn spike from add-on onboarding. Mitigation: Include onboarding checklist and optional concierge setup for first-month customers
